sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
You'll learn how to create and use them like a pro.

• How to declare and initialize 2D arrays
• Accessing elements with row and column indices
• Practical ways to use them in real programs

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine a chessboard - that's a perfect real-world example of a 2D array! Each square has a row and column position, just like elements in a 2D array.

A 2D array is simply an array of arrays. Think of it like:
• A grid with rows and columns
• A table where you can store data in organized rows
• A way to represent game boards, images, or spreadsheets

For example, this creates a 3x3 grid:
```java
int[][] grid = new int[3][3];
```
• First number = rows (like floors in a building)
• Second number = columns (like rooms on each floor)

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Access a 2D array element with two indices: matrix[row][column]
matrix.length returns the number of rows; matrix[0].length returns columns in the first row
Initialize with nested braces: int[][] m = {{1,2},{3,4},{5,6}}
Default values are 0 for numeric types and null for object types
Array indices are zero-based: the first element is at [0][0]

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: 2D arrays store data in rows and columns like a grid. Use [row][column] to access elements (remember: 0-indexed!) Practice with nested loops to process all elements.

questions.question: Which statement correctly creates a 3x4 two-dimensional integer array?
questions.explanation: The correct syntax is: int[][] arr = new int[3][4]; This creates an array with 3 rows and 4 columns.

questions.question: What does matrix.length return for a 2D array?
questions.explanation: For a 2D array, matrix.length returns the number of rows. To get the number of columns in row i, use matrix[i].length.
